description: We’re Cosmic Challengers, a Thrissur-based team tackling “Abandoned but Not Forgotten”: telling the stories of NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars through an engaging, interactive experience. Having just curiosity and the willingness to learn. Join us and give forgotten machines a voice!
summary: Still Out There is a story-driven website for school students about the robots NASA left in space: Surveyor 3, Mars Pathfinder, Spirit and Opportunity, Ingenuity and Pioneer 10. Students chat with each spacecraft and take a quiz. Each robot gets a “signal lost” moment, so students feel why these machines matter instead of memorising dates. Our aim is to show that “abandoned” does not mean “failed,” and to make space history something young people remember and share. It is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript (canvas animation and Web Audio sound), works on phones and laptops, and uses NASA mission records and photos with credit. We chose a story format, simple language and big visuals so younger students can use it without help.
details:
Our project is a story-driven website for school students about the robots NASA left in space: Surveyor 3, Mars Pathfinder, Spirit and Opportunity, Ingenuity and Pioneer 10. Students chat with each and take a quiz. Each robot gets a “signal lost” moment, so students feel why these machines mattered instead of memorising dates.

Benefits and impact: it turns space history into a story that children can feel and share, and it shows that “abandoned” does not mean “failed.” These robots finished their jobs and changed what we know about the Moon, Mars and deep space.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single file, with canvas animation and Web Audio sound effects, hosted on Netlify. It works on phones and laptops with no sign-up.

Creativity: We used simple language and big visuals so younger students can use it alone.

Factors we considered: accuracy (facts and photos from NASA Science, credited on the site), age-appropriate wording, mobile use .
